title: Five Checks Before You Book a New Carrier
content: After 18 years brokering freight, I run the same five checks on every new carrier. Authority, insurance, safety rating, references, and a real phone call. Skip one and you are asking for trouble.
excerpt: The carrier vetting routine we use at WFS.

title: Why Agricultural Freight Needs a Different Playbook
content: Hauling grain and produce is not the same as auto parts. Seasonality, reefer capacity, and tight delivery windows change how we book. Here is how WFS handles ag lanes through the Southeast and Midwest.

title: DOT Compliance Is the Floor, Not the Ceiling
content: Meeting FMCSA minimums keeps you legal. It does not keep your freight safe. Here is the pre-booking compliance checklist my team runs ahead of every quarterly DOT webinar.

title: Draft: Reading a Carrier Safety Score

title: Smoking Brisket the Night Before a Big Cook
content: Off-topic from freight, but folks keep asking. I start my brisket the night before on the brick pit out back. Low and slow, wrap at the stall, and rest a full hour. Patience is the whole recipe.
excerpt: A pitmaster note from the patio.

title: Reading a Carrier Safety Score the Right Way
content: Most shippers glance at a star rating and stop. The BASIC scores tell you far more about a carrier's real risk. Here is how I weigh unsafe driving, hours of service, and maintenance when I vet.

title: Building Materials Freight in Summer Storm Season
content: East Tennessee summer storms can sit a flatbed load of lumber for a full day. We plan tarping, delivery windows, and detention up front so building supply clients are not caught off guard.

title: Understanding Freight Settlements and Quick Pay
content: Carriers ask about quick pay every week. Here is how a settlement actually flows at WFS, what a quick pay fee covers, and when waiting on standard terms makes more sense for your cash flow.

title: Why We Still Pick Up the Phone
content: Load boards and portals are fine, but freight is still a relationship business. A two-minute call with a carrier tells me more than any rating ever will. That is how WFS has run since 2008.

title: Q3 Capacity Update for Ag Shippers
content: Reefer and hopper capacity is tightening early this year. If you ship grain or produce out of the valley, get your Q3 lanes booked now. We are holding equipment for our regular ag cooperative clients.
excerpt: Book ag lanes early this year.

title: Five Questions to Ask Before You Sign a Broker
content: Shippers ask how to pick a broker. Ask about authority and bond, how they vet carriers, who answers when freight goes sideways, claims history, and references. A good broker welcomes every one.
